description:
Hi! I'm Aayush, a Grade 10 student, independent app, website, and game developer. I'm passionate about technology, coding, innovation, and space exploration.
I'm building a team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge where we can combine our skills, share creative ideas, and develop an innovative solution to a real-world challenge.
summary:
we developed Ares Protocol, an interactive 3D browser-based space mission simulator designed to train young students as junior astronauts managing a lunar or Martian outpost.

To address the challenge, our application translates complex spaceflight engineering into hands-on gameplay. Using real-time NASA telemetry and interactive 3D environments, students actively balance critical survival systems—including life support, radiation shielding, power generation, and food production—while deploying rovers and maintenance drones to overcome off-world hazards.

This project is important because it bridges the gap between theoretical space science and practical problem-solving. By turning abstract aerospace concepts into an accessible, engaging simulation, it sparks curiosity, builds systems-thinking skills, and inspires the next generation of explorers to understand what it truly takes to sustain human life beyond Earth.
details:
Our project is an interactive educational application designed to help young students understand the challenges of building and managing a lunar or Martian outpost.

The application explains important space mission systems such as life support, radiation protection, power management, and food production. It helps students understand how astronauts depend on different systems to survive in space.

The main aim of our project is to make space science easier, more interesting, and accessible to young learners through technology and interactive learning.

We developed this project using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with AI-assisted coding support. Our team focused on creating a simple, user-friendly design and an educational experience.

This project encourages scientific thinking, creativity, problem-solving, and awareness of future space exploration.
